main_argument_chains.claim: KRETP has conditional performance advantages that require density- and feasibility-aware policy interpretation.
support_steps: Run M1 across density and Vmax regimes.
Use M3/M4 to check the shared flow-density pattern.
Compare SCTR and FDFO on the same metric bundle.
Separate median-control improvement from the conceptual centralized extension.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Retain KRETP as the baseline policy, use selective fast/slow separation for recurrent congestion, and treat intelligent control as a bounded future extension.

main_argument_chains.claim: The reported Vmax=5 is a within-model, preference-conditioned selection rather than a universal speed-limit fact.
support_steps: Set light/heavy/mixed scenarios and stated weights.
Translate over/under-posted cases into regime-specific tradeoffs.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Report the selected Vmax with its weights, density regimes, proxy scales, and calibration limits.

warnings.warning: The printed single-lane continuity equation differentiates u rather than rho, unlike the two-lane conservation form.
Sij source prose and net-inflow notation leave direction semantics ambiguous.
Qe is defined with lane density but later used as a function of average density.
rho_h and Delta rho_h occur in the initial condition without supplied values or definitions.
The CA/PDE comparison cites Figure 9 instead of the Figure 11 flow-density relation.
The claimed Wagner-derived rule points to a different textbook reference.
The energy simplification omits conditions and absolute physical scale required by the displayed reduction.
Table, formula, and code leave per-lane versus total Q aggregation unresolved.
Appendix defaults differ from prose and missing coef.prn controls actual experiment configuration.
Median-control curves omit the seed, controller configuration, and repeat uncertainty despite small visible differences.
Coordinated queue release is conceptual and lacks a constrained control algorithm or experiment.
SCTR mixture is explicit but source does not establish exact lane assignments or repeated scenario protocol.
Completed CA cell/time physical calibration is absent, so simulated Vmax cannot be treated as a real-world speed limit.

visualization_dispositions.analytical_purpose: Six visually separated Summary paragraphs provide a scanable route from policy question to dual models, metrics, comparisons, control extension, and limitations.
Illustrates default right-lane driving, temporary left-lane overtaking, and return behavior before assumptions and formalization.
Maps the particle-hopping model to a two-column road lattice with vehicles and movement directions.
Plots CA traffic flow Q against density n and supports the low-density increase, capacity peak, and high-density decline discussion.
Plots the alpha_safe proxy against density with explicit lower-is-safer direction.
Plots average energy proxy E0 against density and is paired with its acceleration-based definition.
Shows light-traffic weighted-objective response across maximum-speed candidates.
Shows heavy-traffic weighted-objective response across maximum-speed candidates.
Shows the 4:1 mixed-traffic weighted-objective scan supporting the reported Vmax=5 selection.
CA low-density time-space visualization with time bottom-to-top and motion left-to-right.
CA high-density time-space visualization used to contrast congestion texture.
PDE steady-state fast-lane, slow-lane, and average flow curves against average density.
Low-density PDE dynamics when a cluster first appears in the fast lane.
Low-density PDE dynamics when a cluster first appears in the slow lane.
Higher-density PDE evolution showing instability and stop-and-go behavior.
Three-rule traffic-flow comparison over density.
Three-rule safety-proxy comparison over density, retaining lower-is-safer direction.
Three-rule energy-proxy comparison over density.
Median control flowchart: compare vehicle speed to fleet median and randomize ties.
Equipped versus not-equipped traffic-flow comparison for median control.
Equipped versus not-equipped safety-proxy comparison for median control.
Equipped versus not-equipped energy-proxy comparison for median control.
Illustrates the local-information bottleneck used to motivate conceptual centralized release control.
Defines particle-hopping positions, speeds, current/other-lane gaps, Q, alpha_safe, L, T, probabilities, density, and N.
Specifies acceleration and random deceleration conditions.
Specifies safety, Rule #0, and Rule #1 lane-change conditions.
Maps right-to-left and left-to-right changes to safety plus Rule #0/#1.
Provides the 18-step Monte Carlo input-output and update procedure.
C++ source exposes random vehicle generation, speed assignment, and default global parameters; it is reproducibility evidence, not positive language evidence.
C++ state update implements acceleration, front-gap limitation, random deceleration, cyclic movement, and energy accumulation.
C++ rule_s, rule0, rule1, median, and chLaneSim expose the executable lane-change and median-control branches.
